transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I guess I'm here because I've just been having a little trouble with... well, staying organized, I guess? I mean, I know everyone gets a little scatterbrained sometimes, right? But... well, what finally made me come in is that I keep forgetting just really basic adult things. Like, um, paying my bills on time, or... returning emails for job interviews. 

I just finished my bachelor's degree, so I really need to be on top of that stuff, but I keep showing up late or completely missing appointments, and just not following through on simple errands. I'm really trying my best, I promise, it's just... it's started costing me some real opportunities lately, and I feel terrible about it. I just want to be a little better at managing things. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's an okay reason to come in.
Did you have these kinds of problems with organization or forgetfulness when you were a child?

Um, yeah, I guess so... but I mean, I wasn't, like, a bad kid or anything! My teachers always said I was really bright, which was nice of them. It's just... well, even back in elementary school, they'd write on my report cards that I was a little bit... enthusiastic, maybe? Like I would talk out of turn sometimes, or rush through the directions because I just wanted to get to the fun part. 

And, um, I did lose things a lot. Worksheets and stuff. My desk was always a bit of a disaster zone, honestly, to the point where I couldn't always find my assignments when it was time to turn them in. I tried to keep it clean, I really did, but it just sort of happened. 

I know that probably sounds awful, but I promise I was always trying to be good. Is it normal for kids to be like that? I hope it's not too bad.
Do these problems with organization and follow-through happen in more than one part of your life, like both at work or school and at home?

Um, yeah, I guess it does happen in a few different areas... I mean, I try really hard to keep it all together, but it just sort of spills over. Like, at home, things are a little messy, but nothing too crazy! But... well, it's also affecting my professional life, I suppose. 

I actually... um, I lost my last job recently. It wasn't anything malicious, I promise! I just had a hard time keeping up with the day-to-day tasks. And since then, I've been trying so hard to find something new, but I keep missing the follow-up emails for interviews. I even had to step back from this volunteer project that I really, really loved, just because I couldn't seem to stay on top of the schedule. 

So now I'm unemployed, and I just feel like I'm struggling to manage the basic steps of, you know, being an adult and moving forward. I'm really sorry if that sounds pathetic. I'm trying my best to fix it, I really am. Do you think that's something we can work on?
Do you find yourself having to check or repeat things over and over, even when you know they probably don’t need it?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I do that. I might double-check my alarm sometimes because I'm so worried about being late, but... no, I don't have to keep checking things over and over like that. I usually just kind of do things and move on, maybe a little too quickly sometimes! But I don't get stuck repeating things. Is that a good thing? I hope that's the right answer.
Did these difficulties get much worse after you lost your job?

Um, well... I guess they've been pretty consistent for a while now. I mean, they didn't just suddenly start when I was let go. It's been, gosh, maybe about a year and two months that it's been really, really hard? 

It actually started getting bad back when I was still at the biotech job, right around the time things started falling apart there. I was trying so hard to keep up, but it was just slipping away. And then, of course, it just kind of continued after they had to let me go. I really didn't want to admit how much I was struggling back then, because I wanted them to think I was capable, you know? 

I hope it's okay that it's been going on that long. I should have probably asked for help sooner, but I just kept thinking I could fix it myself. Does that make sense?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I've been feeling depressed. I get a little bummed out sometimes, you know, just because of the job stuff and feeling like I'm not doing as well as I should be. But I try to stay positive! I really do try to look on the bright side and keep a smile on my face. 

I definitely don't feel down most days. I mean, I still get up and try to get things done, even if I struggle with the follow-through part. I'm not, like, staying in bed all day crying or anything like that. I hope that's what you mean? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. I'm really trying to be helpful!
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task or on what someone is saying, even when you want to pay attention?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really do try my best to pay attention, I promise I do! But sometimes, um, like if I sit down to try and update my resume or, you know, work on a coding practice problem... it's just, it's hard. 

Like, if my phone buzzes with a text, or if I hear someone talking outside my window, or even if I just have a random thought pop into my head about something else I need to do... suddenly I'm just completely off track. And I usually don't even realize it happened until later. 

I feel really bad about it, because I know I should just be able to focus and get it done. I'm really trying to get better at it! Does that... does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to be honest with you.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I try really hard not to be a worrier! Obviously, I think about, you know, needing to find a new job and things like that, but I don't just sit around stressing about things if there isn't a real reason to. 

I try to be pretty easygoing, mostly so I don't bother anyone else with my stress. I hope that's a good thing? I really just try to take things as they come and not overthink the future too much. Is that the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am.
